pages.text:
Yash Tailor | Morgan Stanley | On-Campus | FTE
Allowed Branches : CS, IT, Tronics, TC, Trical and MCA
Online Test
-
Section 1 : General Aptitude (Data Interpretation, Numerical Reasoning, Logical Reasoning) 10
Questions in 20 minutes
-
Section 2 : General Computer Science Questions on DSA, OS, DBMS, Networks (20 Questions
in 20 Minutes)
-
Section 3 : Debugging (Finding Logical, Syntax Errors and Completing Functions using
existing ones) 7 Questions in 20 Minutes
-
Section 4 : Coding Questions (Map + Sorting + Graph) 3 Questions in 60 Minutes
-
Q1 The question was fuzzy but the gist was given the list of items, print the unique
items in the same order.
-
TC : O(N), SC : O(N)
-
Q2 Given an array, find the number of ways we can partition the array into three parts,
such that Sum(First Part) <= Sum(Second Part) <= Sum(Third Part)
-
TC : O(NLogN), SC : O(1)
-
Q3 Find the number of single cycle components in the graph.
-
TC : O(V+E), SC : O(V)
After the online test, 34 of us were selected for online interviews.
Round 1 (1 Hour 40 Minutes )
-
Describe in general, your experiences, your contribution, etc.
-
Explain Polymorphism and its types (Both Compile Time - Function Overloading and Operator
Overloading, Run Time - Virtual Functions) and also added vptr and vtable to the discussion.
We also talked about base and derived class pointers and why base can hold derived class
objects and why visa versa being not true.
-
We talked about Inheritance, its types, access specifiers, its effect in the derived class and so
on. Different scenarios were also provided and had to answer them like say the effect of base
class protected members in its child class and corresponding grand child class, etc.
-
We talked about hashing, what is hashing, why to use it, will two complex objects have same
hash (here I added the time concept that if we use time as a parameter while hashing, then it
would be different, this further lead to discussion of consideration of time in hashing and we

talked about blockchain too, here I talked about the necessity of considering time in
blockchain to produce the required complexity in bitcoin)
-
We talked about Pagination (Here I thought he was talking about pagination in terms of web
sites but actually he wanted to know more in terms of locking). Here we talked about the
difficulties in Contiguous Allocation, what Pagination is and how it is performed and then how
Pagination will help to provide efficient locks. (As in if we have only one page and a process
wants to perform write operation then we need to lock the page to avoid dirty reads due to
which other processes wanting to perform write operations will starve and hence multiple
pages will help us perform write operations efficiently) We discussed about time slicing wrt to
uniprocessor system. This further led to discussion of scheduling in multiprocessor systems.
He asked me to list scheduling algorithms and as I mentioned FCFS too, he asked if it would
be suitable if we have larger processes coming in initially which further led to discussion on
SJF and SRTF.
-
We then talked about Semaphores - Binary and Counting, what semaphore is and how it is
used and asked me to give an example of each. I gave them but he wanted something more,
he further added that if we want multiple DB connections, there we can use counting
semaphores. He asked me for a confirmation and my take on the same.
-
We then moved on to OOP Design - Whatsapp Like Chat Application.
-
Main Requirements - Those who sent messages first should always be shown on the
top (in a queue fashion), Able to send and receive text messages along with the single
tick, double tick and blue tick.
-
He asked me to design a chat app for college students so the number of users will be
around 1000.
-
It was a very long discussion, he asked me to design how the data will be stored, and
along with that he asked me to write SQL queries for showing top 10 chats and to
retrieve all the messages for a given friend.
-
We also talked about where we should use what kind of mechanism(push/pull) at the
receiver and client side.
-
Finally, he asked me a coding problem. Given an array of stock prices, find the maximum profit
that can be made by buying and selling only once, not on the same day. Due to time
constraints, I directly gave them the optimal O(N) time complexity, wrote code for the same
on the notepad and explained it with the given example.
-
In between he also asked me if I know maximum subarray sum problem, I said yes so he
moved on saying that then you would also know its algorithm (xD)
-
Asked me if I had any questions. (Asked 3)
After this round, we were left with 14 candidates. (8 EE + 6 AD)

Round 2 (1 Hour and 30 minutes)
-
Deleting the Kth Node from the end of a singly linked list
-
Gave two methods, double and single traversal(two pointer method)
-
Asked me to code on Notepad
-
Mall Parking Lot OOP Design
-
Discussed Requirements (which changed later in the discussion and had to update
the entities), described entities and then asked me to answer the following questions
by developing a data structure and corresponding algorithms in most optimal way:
-
Finding the closest empty spot for a given type of vehicle
-
Finding the location of a vehicle
-
Finding the total amount earned in last 24 hours
-
More focus was on data structure and algorithms
-
3 kinds of vehicles, scooter requires 1 slot, car requires 2 slots and bus requires 4 slots.
-
My final solution was a 2D array (floors X slots)
-
For #1, I gave a linear approach then I tried using linked list, map, stack, etc but
nothing seemed to work that efficiently. He asked me to mention all the data
structures I knew, but I forgot to add heap and I believe heap is the one which can
give the optimal solution (logn time). He liked my LL approach (Keeping the links in
such a way that it always points to an empty spot).
-
For #2, I used a map, map[vehicle_id] = floor_no*number_of_slots + slot_no. Here, if we
divide by number_of_slots, we get the floor no. and the remainder will give slot_no.
-
For #3, I had an entity called Logs, where I can have a pointer to the last log that is
valid till the current time, whenever a query is made, I can move the pointer ahead
from that point till it reaches that specific log whose difference is less than equal to 24
hours so I can take the difference directly (total_num_logs - current_log_number),
also I can move the pointer when a new log is inserted so as to be proactive.
-
Finally he asked me if I had any questions (asked 2)
Now, we were left with 6 candidates (5 EE + 1 AD)

Round 3 (1 Hour)
-
Discussion about my 2020 Internship. Explained the project and my role. Asked a lot of cross
questions and few scaling questions as well.
-
Shoppers Stop OOP Design
-
Given a cart with 10 items and 1 item with 5 quantities, design a data structure to find
the total amount and total discount in such a way that we only consider the items in
the cart where its maximum possible discount doesn’t go beyond a given threshold.
-
Asked me to list all the entities and their data properties. Again more focus was on
data structures and algorithms. Here we talked about how data will be stored and
retrieved and how efficiently we can perform all the calculations.
-
He then asked if there is an offer that is valid for only 10 minutes, how would you go
about implementing that. Here, again storing data and the algorithm was given more
preference.
-
It was a long discussion, I asked a lot of questions for clarification as the problem was
very general and he was asking to optimize it but that can only be performed if I get
more specific details.
-
Few more questions which I don’t remember.
-
HR Questions
-
Scenario where I faced conflict and how did I resolved it (gave 2 examples)
-
Scenario where I did something unethical and how did I resolved it (gave 1 funny
example)
-
Asked me if I had any questions (asked 2)
Finally 5 of us got selected (3 BTech + 2 MCA) (4 EE + 1 AD)
Note : There were 2 tracks  - Application Dev (AD) and Enterprise Engineering (EE). I was a part of AD
track.
Fun Part : 6 of us were called again to fill the application form for FTE and were sent back. An hour
later we were called again for the results.
PS : It's gonna be a very long day, stay patient, calm, hydrated and make sure you are not hungry. Stay
confident!
Observation : In OOP Design, they don’t look for the exact right answers, our approach, the way we
discuss, and our thinking process matters a lot, basically our efforts.
